title: Cores, the scheduler and a context switch
desc: A drawing of a queue of ready threads from several processes, a small number of cores that can each run one of them, and what the kernel saves and restores when it changes who is running.

steps.note: The phone has a fixed number of cores. Each one runs exactly one thread at a time.
Every thread that is ready to run waits in one list, from every app on the device.
The scheduler picks which of them get the cores right now. It schedules threads, not processes.
When a turn ends, the kernel saves that thread's registers, program counter and stack pointer.
If the next thread belongs to another process, the page table is swapped too, and that costs more.
Coroutines are objects on your heap. They never enter this list, and a suspended one holds no thread.
